entities.summary:
Vitellozzo Vitelli was an Italian condottiero who played a pivotal role in the Italian Wars of the 15th century. He was born into a noble family and trained as a soldier from a young age, eventually becoming a prominent military leader in his own right. Vitelli's military campaigns took him across central Italy, where he clashed with powerful city-states and foreign armies. He was known for his bravery and tactical genius, earning him the respect of his contemporaries and the admiration of later historians. Vitelli's legacy as a military leader and statesman has endured for centuries, with his name becoming synonymous with Italian Renaissance militarism. His influence can still be seen in modern military strategy and tactics, and his life has been the subject of numerous historical studies and literary works. The city of Montone, where Vitelli was born and raised, remains a testament to his enduring legacy, with numerous monuments and historical sites dedicated to his memory.

Vitellozzo Vitelli was a central figure in the Italian Wars, a complex and multifaceted conflict that involved many of the major city-states of Italy. He was a key player in the wars, leading his troops into battle against the forces of Milan, Florence, and the Papal States. Vitelli's military campaigns were marked by their brutality and intensity, as he sought to expand his own power and influence in central Italy. Despite his formidable military skills, Vitelli was ultimately killed in battle in 1503, marking the end of an era in Italian military history.
